summary: Redwood AE/SE walked the SouthBay platform team through org/project key model for multi-tenant rate limits and quotas, demonstrated Console controls for per-project throttles, burst policies, and global org quotas. Customer cares about per-tenant isolation, SSO/SAML, KMS encryption, and predictable pricing for peak clinical hours. Agreement to run a short POC and share security docs.
transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-06-10 15:00 PDT  Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (Redwood CSM); Mark Chen (SouthBay CTO), Aisha Patel (Head of Platform), Liam O'Connor (Security), Nora Kim (PM)

00:00 Jordan Lee: hey everyone thanks for joining, we're excited to walk through the rate limits and org/project keys setup, um Priya will drive the demo and i'll cover pricing and next steps
00:12 Mark Chen: thanks jordan, quick context - we run multi-tenant APIs for clinical notes, peak windows around 08:00-11:00 and 18:00-21:00, we need per-customer quotas and ability to throttle heavy tenants without affecting others
00:28 Priya Nair: great, that's exactly what the org/project keys model solves. i'll share my screen  ok loading console, bear with me
00:45 Priya Nair: so top-level is the Org quota, you can set monthly or daily token caps, then projects inherit or get bespoke limits. important bit: you can map a project to a customer id and attach rate-limits and billing rules
01:10 Aisha Patel: is there a hard concurrency limit per project? we saw in some vendors they only do token based and not concurrency
01:21 Priya Nair: good question. we support multiple limit dimensions  tokens, requests per minute, and concurrency. concurrency limits are enforced at the runtime level and you can pick enforcement policy; soft throttle with queue vs hard reject
01:40 Liam O'Connor: what about burst behavior? sometimes some tenants spike for a few minutes and we want graceful degradation
01:50 Priya Nair: we have a burst bucket capacity you can configure per project or org. you can also enable adaptive burst smoothing  it will allow short spikes while respecting longer-term quotas
02:10 Jordan Lee: and on billing alignment you can bill the tenant for overage or have a cost-center chargeback; we expose per-project usage by token type in the Console and via API
02:32 Nora Kim: can we tie limits to API keys we issue to our clients? we want to hand out keys ourselves, not Redwood-managed keys
02:45 Priya Nair: absolutely  there's two modes: Redwood-managed project keys or customer-managed keys. for customer-managed you can bring your own project id and we accept a signed token; that works well with your existing key rotation
03:05 Mark Chen: security compliance  KMS + encryption at rest, and audit trails  do you persist requests or PII in logs?
03:17 Carlos Mendes: quick note from CSM  we default to minimal retention for hosted, and can support VPC/private deployments with on-prem retention controls. Priya will show where audit logs live
03:28 Priya Nair: here in the Console, audit logs show key creation, policy changes, and per-route access. logs are exportable to your SIEM or to S3. for encryption we can integrate with customer KMS (GCP/AWS/Azure or HSM)
03:50 Liam O'Connor: SSO for admin console? we use SAML and have strict RBAC
03:58 Priya Nair: yes, SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning and granular RBAC by project and org. you can restrict who can change quotas vs who can view usage
04:15 Priya Nair: switching to demo  creating a new project  name, map to tenant id, attach billing center, then set defaults: request rpm 2000, concurrency 20, token daily cap 50k
04:40 Priya Nair: show the policy chains  you can have an org-level fallback bucket and then project-level overrides; when a request arrives we evaluate project policy then org fallback, then global defaults
05:05 Mark Chen: if a project hits quota do we 429 or queue? can we choose?
05:13 Priya Nair: you choose per-policy. options: hard reject (429), queue up to N seconds, or redirect to a cheaper model variant. we often recommend queue for user-facing sync calls and hard reject for background jobs
05:29 Nora Kim: cheaper model variant  is that automatic? like fall back from an LLM-70b to 13b?
05:36 Priya Nair: you can configure automatic fallbacks by latency or cost thresholds  e.g., under heavy load route to a quantized 13b or an efficient embedding-based rerank. it's policy-driven
05:50 Jordan Lee: many customers use that to control unit economics during spikes; Redwood Optimize gives suggestions on which model variants to use per workload
06:05 Mark Chen: curious on enforcement latency  is rate-limit decision in the hot path? we can't add >10ms overhead to each call
06:15 Priya Nair: good point. enforcement is a lightweight check at the edge, often sub-millisecond if you use the local proxy. for private deployments we can run the rate limiting locally to avoid network hop
06:34 Aisha Patel: for POC we'd like per-tenant dashboards and real-time alerts if a tenant crosses 80% quota
06:42 Priya Nair: you can create alert rules in Console tied to thresholds and webhook to your PagerDuty or Slack; dashboards can be per-project and token-type filtered
06:55 Mark Chen: what's the integration path with our billing system? we want a CSV/stream of usage per tenant per day
07:05 Jordan Lee: we export usage via API and scheduled CSV exports; we can also push to your datawarehouse via event stream. we'll include the usage schema in the docs we send
07:18 Liam O'Connor: legal requested the network diagram and details on private deployment. do you support on-prem with HSM?
07:26 Carlos Mendes: yes, Private supports on-prem and VPC, can integrate with your HSM for key material and we provide a hardened control plane. i'll attach the network diagram and the SLOs in the follow-up
07:38 Priya Nair: jumping back to demo  show rate-limit metrics view, you can see tokens/sec, request latency, rejects and queued requests, filter by project
08:10 Nora Kim: how do we map our internal customer id to Redwood project id? do you have an API for mapping?
08:18 Priya Nair: yes there's a simple mapping endpoint and you can push metadata like tier and SLA. mappings are immutable once created to avoid accidental reassignment, but you can create a new project and migrate
08:36 Mark Chen: around quotas - we have unpredictable seasonal spikes. can we set scheduled overrides to increase quotas during expected windows?
08:46 Priya Nair: scheduled policies are supported. you can define calendar-based overrides for holidays, backups, or marketing events. those overrides are applied before on-the-fly burst buckets
09:05 Jordan Lee: quick pricing note  reserved capacity for Dedicated reduces per-token unit cost and you can have committed burst pools. we'll share concrete numbers in the spreadsheet
09:18 Priya Nair: demo part 2  API side: here's the project key in header X-Project-Key, we validate and fetch policy, then route to model runtime. here's a curl example
09:36 Priya Nair: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'X-Project-Key: sbh-1234' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"..."}'
09:50 Mark Chen: what about client-side SDKs to enforce local rate-limits for graceful backoff? we have mobile clients too
09:58 Priya Nair: we provide client libraries with circuit-breaker and retry helpers and recommend a small leaky-bucket client-side to smooth spikes; server side still authoritative
10:20 Aisha Patel: if we self-host keys, how do you reconcile usage for billing?
10:28 Jordan Lee: usage is tied to project id; whether keys are customer-managed or Redwood-managed doesn't affect metering  we still report per-project aggregates to your billing endpoint
10:45 Liam O'Connor: auditability  can we run periodic attestation of key rotations and access logs?
10:53 Carlos Mendes: yes, audit exports and we can enable immutable logs in Private deployments; for hosted we retain for configurable window and exports are available for audits
11:08 Priya Nair: running a quick scenario  tenant A spikes, hits request rpm, burst bucket consumes, then fallback to 13b is triggered and a webhook alert fires. walk through sim now
11:30 Priya Nair: simulation result  92% requests served, 6% queued (avg 300ms extra), 2% rejected. you can tune the queue length and fallback policy until you meet SLAs
12:00 Mark Chen: ok that simulation looks promising. for the POC we'd like real traffic replay from our logs to validate latency and cost
12:12 Priya Nair: good, we support traffic replay  we'll want a sanitized subset. Priya -> we'll run replay in dedicated POC cluster to capture metrics
12:30 Jordan Lee: recap and next steps: we'll send pricing spreadsheet + security pack, Priya will prepare POC runbook, you will share sample traffic and SSO details, agree to POC kickoff on 2026-06-16
12:48 Mark Chen: sounds good. thanks everyone
12:52 Jordan Lee: thanks all, we'll follow up and send materials
13:00 Meeting end.

Notes on transcript: occasional mis-transcriptions and shorthand in the UI lines, proper nouns like some product names may be slightly off (e.g., Redwood Optimize transcribed as Redwood Optimise).
